name: Grammar And Clarity Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on grammar and clarity so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on grammar and clarity so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting grammar and clarity work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. State assumptions about grammar and clarity explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
3. Measure before optimizing any grammar and clarity bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. When multiple grammar and clarity strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Prefer the simplest grammar and clarity approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Check that grammar and clarity terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. When grammar and clarity guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
8. Prefer explicit, readable grammar and clarity solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen grammar and clarity approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
10. Keep grammar and clarity changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop grammar and clarity edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic grammar and clarity advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of grammar and clarity correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated grammar and clarity concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about grammar and clarity over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
